preregistration.study: context_lever -- break the 66.4% chat gold-store ceiling with information the question does not carry

corpus.why: temporal_bench does not predict deployment; chat_bench_v2 does (binding finding, DECISIONS.md / chat_target_decision.md)

split.rule: every hyper-parameter (N, theta, alpha, mu, tau, merge_k, mode, placement) is chosen on dev; test is scored ONCE with frozen configs and never swept

metric.primary: top1_sub -- expected_substring inside the rank-1 text
metric.arm: gold store (perfect write gate), i.e. ladder rung L1

B1.name: shipped engine, gold store
B1.stack: gate=gold, doc tags=shipped detect_entity, direction=shipped inference, query tagger=shipped

B2.name: the corrected 66.4% ceiling stack
B2.stack: gate=gold, direction=true_oracle, oracle doc tags, achievable query oracle (tags only where the head is in the question)
B2.caveat: B2 inherits the ladder's oracles, so it is a diagnostic arm: it answers 'does extra information break the ceiling', not 'what ships'. The deployable claim rests on B1.

bar.rule: paired-bootstrap 95% CI lower bound > 0 vs the SAME-stack baseline AND a point estimate >= +5.0 pt

a_conversation_context.ceiling_reported_first: share of questions whose attribute head is present in the prior window at all, and share where the most recently discussed attribute is the right one

b_per_user_attribute_priors.closed_set: the vault's OWN entity table (arena.entity_names), never the fixture's attribute list

c_multi_intent.rule: retrieve for the top-k candidate intents and merge by best score per document
c_multi_intent.equal_budget: top_k=10 returned by every arm and the corpus is scanned exhaustively either way; the extra cost is k ranking passes, reported as scan_multiplier

firing_policy.fallback: the mechanism speaks only when the arm's own tagger is silent (the engine's _resolve_intent finds no intent the vault knows) -- the deployable shape
firing_policy.override: the mechanism always speaks; swept on dev as a control

leak_audit.barrier_1: resolvers receive a QueryView exposing .text only; every other field (qid, gold_fid, expected_substring, type, head_survives_query, attribute) raises LeakViolation and is counted
leak_audit.barrier_2: the context window drops the gold turn and any turn containing the expected substring; the audit recounts both over the turns actually handed out and RAISES if non-zero
leak_audit.barrier_3: every frozen parameter is asserted numeric/bool/whitelisted so no dev question text or label can ride into test (chat_bench_v2 reuses elided phrasings across personas -- the exact channel that leaked in the withdrawn oracle)
leak_audit.barrier_4: negative controls: shuffled_context (each question gets another question's window) and foreign_view (the resolver gets another persona's vault). A gain that survives these is not the information it claims to be
leak_audit.barrier_5: on B2 the achievable oracle is built per persona from the one phrasing in use with collisions dropped, and the audit RAISES if any head-dropped question received an oracle tag

quarantine.how: quarantine_guard.enforce() wraps builtins.open / io.open / os.open / os.fdopen / numpy.load in THIS process
quarantine.atime: not cited -- measured on this volume, reads do not bump atime
quarantine.pytest: this study does not run pytest, so it does not trigger the nanomem test that opens the held-out fixture

amendments_after_the_pilot_run.why: a pilot of this pipeline reached the test split and then died inside its own negative control (audit_raise() caught the control handing a question its own gold turn). No results file was written, but six test numbers had been printed -- they are listed verbatim in test_phase.__doc__ so nothing is hidden.
changed: the (c) dev grid was widened to unthresholded merges, the only setting where a k-way merge can see k candidates
the shuffled_context control re-applies the receiving question's exclusions (a leak fix forced by the audit)
theta and merge_k were made orthogonal, so mechanism (c) can merge more than one intent instead of silently collapsing to k=1

the ceiling (B2) arm is frozen from its own B2 dev sweep with FALLBACK firing, instead of inheriting B1's override config: overriding an oracle tagger with a guess is incoherent. The override variant is still scored and reported

two diagnostics were added that cannot win anything: an ORACLE-SELECTOR rung (perfect selection among the window's own candidates, dev only, an upper bound on mechanism (a)) and a redundancy split (tag accuracy where the baseline was already right vs where it was wrong)
amendments_after_the_pilot_run.not_changed: no arm's configuration and no freeze rule was chosen using a test number; the pipeline is seeded and deterministic, so arms common to both runs reproduce exactly (B1 52.3%, B2 66.7%, (a) 49.0%, (b) 53.3%, (d) 50.7% in both)

pre_registered_failure_modes: a wrong tag costs accuracy: the intent boost hoists the wrong revision group, so a mechanism can lose questions it used to win
a window large enough to contain the head contains every other attribute too, so coverage and selectivity trade off
the pseudo-relevance prior can only re-assert what cosine already believes; its value, if any, is that it switches the temporal/revision layer on for a question that never names its attribute

engine_fingerprint.note: nanomem/ was under concurrent edit by another agent during this run; these hashes are what was imported

barrier_self_test.barrier_2_and_5_audit: raised: ARM 'self_test' (self_test split) LEAKED: 1 context windows contained the gold turn; 1 context windows contained the expected answer; 1 resolver reads of a forb

ladder_conversion.note: upper bounds: they assume a correct tag always converts and a wrong tag never costs anything, neither of which is true

B1.note: a high overlap means foreign_view swaps in a nearly identical closed set, so it cannot destroy much -- read the control accordingly

B2.note: a high overlap means foreign_view swaps in a nearly identical closed set, so it cannot destroy much -- read the control accordingly

reproduces_published_ladder.source: chat_target_decision.json test300 rungs L1 and L3

audit_summary.note: every counter is checked PER ARM by audit_raise(), which raises LeakViolation instead of reporting; this run completed, so every per-arm count was zero (the foreign_view control is exempt from the vocab check by construction -- that is what it tests)

verdict.statement: No mechanism cleared the pre-registered +5.0 pt bar.

one_ceiling_first.claim: the attribute head is almost never in a SHORT prior window, and the most recently discussed attribute is almost never the one being asked about
one_ceiling_first.consequence: mechanism (d) is dead on arrival on this corpus, and mechanism (a) can only work at a window size where the window IS the closed set -- at which point it is mechanism (b)

four_the_ceiling_is_selection_bounded_no.claim: the information IS in the vault: with perfect selection among the candidate attributes the session itself names, the ceiling stack moves well past 66.4% on dev
four_the_ceiling_is_selection_bounded_no.what_the_oracle_supplies: only WHICH of the ~22 attributes the session already names is the right one -- no value, no document, no direction
four_the_ceiling_is_selection_bounded_no.not_deployable: it is a bound, not a mechanism: an implementable selector would have to make that choice from the elided question, and every similarity-based selector measured here fails at it

five_why_the_selectors_fail.claim: the recovered attribute is redundant with what the retriever already believed: the selector is right where the baseline was already right and wrong where it was not
five_why_the_selectors_fail.arm: B2 best_fallback, head-dropped questions, test split
five_why_the_selectors_fail.consequence: a tag that only arrives when it is not needed cannot convert, and the wrong tags it brings with it hoist the wrong revision group, which is why every high-coverage arm loses points

six_read_the_controls_honestly.shuffled_context_note: vacuous for the frozen B1 arm, which does not read the window at all -- it confirms window-independence and nothing more
six_read_the_controls_honestly.reading: another user's closed set does at least as well as this user's, and the two sets overlap heavily, so the PER-USER part of the prior contributes nothing measurable here

recommendation.reason: no mechanism cleared the pre-registered bar, and the two high-coverage ones are significantly negative
recommendation.next_lever: a CLOSED-SET selector for elided questions -- pick one of the 24 attribute names the vault already holds. That is multiple choice, not the open-vocabulary tagging whose ceiling was withdrawn, and the oracle rung says it is worth up to +15.0 pt on the ceiling stack. Embedding similarity does not do it (23.8% on head-dropped questions, and its errors are correlated with the retriever's own). Anything that would do it -- an LLM or a trained cross-encoder over (question, attribute name) -- is outside nanomem's numpy-only runtime and would have to sit in the caller, so the cost is architectural, not incremental.
recommendation.do_not_retry: short context windows, session recency, unthresholded priors, and any arm that overrides a confident tagger -- all measured negative here
